source_events.content: For concurrency bugs, first spell out the state transitions and what must remain true, then reproduce the bug and verify the fix. This helps me review the race.
For reproducible bugs, start with the smallest failing test, make a small fix, verify it, then explain why it works. Concrete feedback helps me review it.

For this single-process preview server, choose the in-process cache to avoid operating another service. We considered Redis but do not need it yet. We expect fewer repeated renders. Revisit the choice if we add independent workers.

At revision example_r1, in the single-process test fixture: two sequential requests for the same unchanged input invoke the renderer once. Test passed. No latency benchmark or concurrent-worker test was run.
The cache size might be causing the slow queries. I propose testing a larger cache. This is a hypothesis.

Synthetic benchmark report: revision example_search_r1, workload fixture Q, 100 requests. Run A used cache 128 MB on machine A and median latency was 80 ms. Run B used cache 512 MB on machine B and median latency was 40 ms. Hardware and cache size both changed. No controlled rerun has occurred.
For preview verification, docs/preview-checks.md is our canonical project guide. Read it when changing the preview renderer. Keep setup commands there rather than making another copy.

In project preview_example, docs/preview-checks.md exists at example_guide_r2. This observation verifies file presence and revision only; host discovery, loading, and command execution have not been checked.

Compare training loss with evaluator eval_v1 on data_v1, lower is better, on GPU_A under a 300-second training budget excluding startup and compilation. This comparison is exploratory, not an adopted architecture decision.

Synthetic report report_runs_v1: baseline commit train_r1 completed on GPU_A with evaluator eval_v1, data_v1, seed 7, budget 300 training seconds excluding startup and compilation, score 1.2. Candidate train_r2 under the same configured conditions crashed with OOM before evaluation; its CSV score is placeholder 0.0 and no valid score exists. No repeated runs or uncertainty estimates.
